Question: Ten chairs are evenly spaced around a round table and numbered clockwise from \(1\) through \(10.\) Five married couples are to sit in the chairs with men and women alternating, and no one is to sit either next to or directly across from his or her spouse. How many seating arrangements are possible?
Solution:
First choose whether the men occupy the odd-numbered or even-numbered chairs. There are \(2\) choices, and the five men can then be placed in their chairs in \(5!=120\) ways.

Fix one placement with men in chairs \(1,3,5,7,9\). Label them \(M_1,M_2,M_3,M_4,M_5\) in that order, and let \(W_i\) be the wife of \(M_i\). Removing the two neighboring chairs and the directly opposite chair leaves these possibilities:
\[
\begin{aligned}
W_1&:4\text{ or }8,\\
W_2&:6\text{ or }10,\\
W_3&:8\text{ or }2,\\
W_4&:10\text{ or }4,\\
W_5&:2\text{ or }6.
\end{aligned}
\]
Choosing \(W_1\)'s seat forces all the others.

If \(W_1\) takes chair \(4\), then \(W_4\) must take \(10\), \(W_2\) must take \(6\), \(W_5\) must take \(2\), and \(W_3\) must take \(8\).

If \(W_1\) takes chair \(8\), then \(W_3\) must take \(2\), \(W_5\) must take \(6\), \(W_2\) must take \(10\), and \(W_4\) must take \(4\).

Both placements satisfy every restriction. They are the only possibilities because \(W_1\) has only those two choices. Shifting every chair number one place clockwise gives the same count when men occupy the even-numbered chairs.

Every arrangement has a unique gender pattern, placement of the men, and placement of the wives. Since the chairs are numbered, rotations remain distinct. Thus the total is
\[
2\cdot5!\cdot2=\boxed{480},
\]
choice \(\text{C}\).
